basic_info.name: CalcLab
basic_info.category: Lab exam interpretation engine (B2B SaaS for health professionals) with a secondary patient-facing pay-per-report web flow
basic_info.country: Brazil (Brasília-DF; founders' education funnel targets PT/BR-speaking nutritionists)
basic_info.stage: Alive, bootstrapped micro-company. Founded Jan/2021 (some sources say 2020) by nutritionist Karla Lacerda (CEO) and pharmacist/biochemist Gabriel de Carvalho (CSO); funded with ~R$1M from the founder selling two properties. Sought a R$7M round in 2022 (Stoic Capital) — no public record it ever closed. LinkedIn shows 2-10 employees, 73 followers. Revenue R$320k (2021), R$1.2M target (2022, unverified). Growth looks flat: the '4,000+ users / 150,000+ exams' site badges match the Aug/2022 press numbers unchanged.
basic_info.pricing_model: Professional SaaS: R$69.90/month, R$335/6-months (-20%), R$503/year (-40%), unlimited exam processing, 15-day free trial, cancel anytime. Patient flow: free reading of identified values, then one-time PIX/credit-card payment for the full report (exact price only shown inside the flow — not published). Course bundling: co-founder's 'Formação em Exames Laboratoriais' / 'Imersão' cohorts have included 3 months of CalcLab access. No recent price changes detected (R$69.99 in mid-2022 press vs R$69.90 today).
basic_info.target_user: Primary: health professionals who interpret exams — nutritionists (especially functional-nutrition audience), pharmacists, biomedicals, nurses, dentists and doctors ('all health professionals want this, not just doctors'). Secondary: lay patients via the homepage flow. Explicitly NOT a patient-app company by design.
basic_info.scale_metrics: Durable-threat read: LOW-MODERATE and flat. Evidence: site badges stuck at 2022 numbers (4k+ active users, 150k+ exams processed; patient homepage says '10k+ exams analyzed'); SimilarWeb Jul/2026 = Brazil rank #324k (global #4.8M), 100% BR traffic, display-ads as #1 acquisition channel, only 34 organic keywords, +14.3% MoM but from a small base; engagement is real though (6min24s avg visit, 5.43 pages, 18.7% bounce) — a used tool, not a ghost town. LinkedIn 73 followers, 2-10 employees. Reclame Aqui has an active complaint track (Feb-Jul/2026) about cancellation, login and unresponsive support — small volume but a churn/support smell. Noise to ignore: the '800+ labs' press claim.

product.core_features: Upload PDF/JPG/PNG/WebP exam; agnostic extraction engine selecting the lab (350+ named on the current /clinica page — Dasa, Fleury, Sabin, Einstein, Lavoisier, Hermes Pardini, Álvaro; 800+ national + international incl. US/Chile/Portugal/Spain/UAE per 2022 press — marketing inconsistent); 200+ clinical rules from indexed international studies with bibliographic references (press has claimed 400+); 'ideal values' instead of lab reference ranges; unit conversion; multi-exam interrelation and derived-index calculation (e.g., HOMA-IR from glucose+insulin+HbA1c); severity alerts; risk flags for future chronic conditions (diabetes etc.); report organized into logical blocks (e.g., 'Hemoglobina e Leucócitos'); patient timeline to compare exams across dates (shipped by 2026 — in 2022 they deliberately deferred it to avoid data-custody liability); specialist-type recommendation (GP, endocrinologist, nutritionist, hematologist).
product.signature_differentiator: The combination no BR patient-app has: (1) a lab-agnostic extraction engine covering hundreds of different lab PDF formats built in-house since 2021, and (2) interpretation against OPTIMAL ('ideal') values with per-rule bibliographic citations — framed as 'hundreds of personalized acceptable ranges' per patient characteristics. Plus a radical data posture: original exam files destroyed right after extraction (they publicly chose NOT to store exams to dodge LGPD custody burden — 'more prudent to avoid the burden and responsibility of storing this data'). The real moat, though, is distribution: the co-founder IS an exam-interpretation educator (Formação de Exames Laboratoriais 2.0, 12 modules; Imersão FSA) and the tool is sold through that course funnel to nutritionists — a self-fueling B2B channel competitors can't copy without an education business.
product.lab_data_handling: Upload-based (PDF or photo; JPG/PNG/WebP accepted). User selects the emitting laboratory from the supported list; engine converts units and normalizes each parameter rather than trusting the lab's printed reference range, then applies ideal-range rules. Processes blood, urine and saliva panels; reads several exams at once and cross-relates them (HOMA-IR example). Professional flow tracks evolution across dates (patient timeline). NO lab integrations/LIS connections, no scheduled retesting cadence, no hardware, no wearables, no CGM — it is a pure interpret/organize layer over whatever PDF the professional already has.
product.family_dependents_depth: None found. Patient characteristics (sex, age, etc.) are entered per-analysis for range personalization, but there is no dependents structure, no caregiver mode, no pediatric bands, no hereditary-risk view. Their own privacy posture (files destroyed after extraction) structurally discourages longitudinal family records — a self-imposed ceiling. This remains an open flank for Dr. Exame's family/caregiver pillar.
product.doctor_sharing: Inverted model: the professional is the USER, not the recipient. No evidence of a patient-to-doctor sharing link, no pre-visit brief, no SOAP export, no CID-10. In the patient flow the 'sharing' artifact is an emailed private link to the lay report, plus specialist-type suggestions ('take this to an endocrinologist'). The consult benefit is indirect: patient 'arrives better prepared for the consultation'. Nothing for the doctor's workflow itself.
product.action_loop_monetization: Post-interpretation action is thin. Patient side: pay once for the report, see specialist recommendations — end of loop; no supplements, no protocols, no telemedicine, no prescriptions. Professional side: the real action loop is EDUCATION — upsell into the founders' courses (Formação 2.0, Imersão FSA) where CalcLab access is bundled, i.e., the tool monetizes the course funnel and vice versa. 2022 roadmap mentioned partnerships for personalized vitamin/supplement lines based on exam results — no evidence it shipped. No marketplace, no pharmacy tie-ins, no affiliate structure visible.

technology.ai_approach: Deterministic rules engine wearing an 'IA' marketing coat: 200-400+ evidence-cited rules + unit conversion + ideal-value bands + multi-marker interrelation, developed in-house. Newer copy says 'AI agent extracts values and applies clinical rules... in seconds', but no LLM, no generative layer, no published model details — processing speed (20s claim in 2022, 'seconds' today) is consistent with rule evaluation, not LLM inference. Human-in-the-loop is explicit: the professional closes the diagnosis ('the platform does not offer the diagnosis, it suggests').
technology.data_inputs: Lab exam PDFs/photos only. Optional patient characteristics (sex, age) to personalize ranges. No wearable ingestion, no genetics (nutrigenetics appears only as course curriculum, not product input), no CGM, no questionnaires, no Health Connect/Apple Health.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: PDF + JPG/PNG/WebP upload across 350-800+ lab layouts (their single deepest asset). Exhaust: on-screen report + emailed private link (patient flow); report output for professionals. NO FHIR, NO Health Connect Medical Records, NO Apple Health Records, NO RNDS/REL, NO LIS/API integrations, NO WhatsApp. Email is the only 'channel' surface. The absence of every modern interoperability rail is the clearest structural gap.
technology.platform: Web only (calclab.com.br patient flow + /clinica professional SaaS; app.calclab.com.br login gated behind Cloudflare). No iOS/Android apps (App Store/Play hits named 'CalcLab' are unrelated calculator apps), no public API, no extension.

ux.onboarding: Patient: email + upload PDF, results identified on-page for free in <3 minutes, full report behind one-time PIX/card paywall, private link by email — no account needed. Professional: 15-day free trial, then subscription. Time-to-value is genuinely short on both; friction is minimal.
ux.data_visualization: Report grouped into logical clinical blocks; flags values outside functional/ideal ranges, alert markers and repeated exams. Cross-marker indices (HOMA-IR). Patient timeline comparing results across dates on the professional side. No scores, no sparklines/trend charts evidenced, no dashboard — text/table report aesthetic, not a data-viz product; depth lives in the written interpretation, not graphics.
ux.engagement_channel: Transactional by design. Patient: one-shot report via email link — classic lab-app open-and-churn pattern; no retention mechanics, no reminders, no WhatsApp. Professional: recurring usage during consultations is the retention loop, reinforced by the course community (Zoom immersions, Instagram reels on thyroid etc.). Acquisition is display-ads + course funnel, NOT SEO (blog literally empty — 'Nenhum artigo publicado ainda'; 34 organic keywords vs Kantesti's aggressive content play). No community, streaks, or nudge system.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Partial transparency: every rule carries a bibliographic reference to indexed international studies — better than nothing, and the founders are credentialed practitioners (nutritionist CEO; pharmacist/biochemist CSO who teaches exam interpretation). BUT: no published accuracy claims, no methodology paper, no clinical board disclosed beyond the founders, no peer review, no external validation. Rules partly authored by the founders themselves. Billing transparency is weak: patient report price hidden until inside the flow; Reclame Aqui complaints (Feb-Jul/2026) cite cancellation difficulty, login failures and unanswered refund requests. Risk list: stale growth metrics presented as current; 350 vs 800+ labs inconsistency; '150 mil assinantes' (150k subscribers) claim in 2022 press that contradicts the 4k active users figure.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Deliberately conservative data posture: LGPD-forward (encryption in transit/at rest, row-level security, files destroyed after extraction), explicit disclaimers on both surfaces — 'not a medical consultation', 'final interpretation and any health decision must be made with a health professional', 'the platform does not offer the diagnosis, it suggests'. Because the professional closes the loop, CalcLab positions as decision-support software for clinicians rather than a patient-facing SaMD — no ANVISA registration/RDC 657 engagement found, no FDA/wellness-line statements needed. The file-destruction choice doubles as regulatory-risk minimization (no health-data custody = smaller LGPD blast radius). Note the tension: destroying files forecloses longitudinal/family products to stay 'safe'.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they DON'T do (= Dr. Exame opportunities): no mobile app, no family/dependents/caregiver mode, no pediatric bands; no engagement loop (nudges, streaks, chat, WhatsApp); no SEO/content play (empty blog, 34 keywords) — the D2C discovery war is winnable; no interoperability rails (FHIR, Health Connect, Apple Health, RNDS); no patient timeline retention due to file-destruction posture; no doctor-facing brief/SOAP/export; no free-forever tier for patients beyond the initial reading. What they DO well (= inspiration, not copy): (1) ideal values vs reference ranges with per-rule bibliography — Dr. Exame already matched this in M3/M4; (2) the education-funnel distribution — Dr. Exame's doctor channel (Atendi/convites) could adopt the 'teach the tool' playbook; (3) pay-per-report PIX pricing as a low-friction D2C SKU the patient homepage proves viable; (4) file-destruction as a marketable privacy posture. Bottom line: CalcLab is a pro-workflow tool with interpretation depth, not a patient product — the D2C threat is real only if they invest in the patient funnel (current traffic says they haven't).
trust_gaps.relevance: HIGH as B2B interpretation benchmark, LOW as D2C threat. They validated the 'ideal values + cited evidence + derived indices (HOMA-IR)' playbook Dr. Exame has now replicated (M1-M5) — but their business gravity is the nutritionist course-funnel at R$69.90/mo (3.5x Dr. Exame's price), not the patient. Monitor: (a) any investment in the patient flow (app, SEO, WhatsApp), (b) whether the 2022 R$7M round ever lands, (c) Reclame Aqui support deterioration.
